workload: RGDS Duke3D 320x200 rendered demo, 60s warmup / 120s capture; no fresh performance comparison or optimization

confirmedStatusPolling.description: VGA port 0x3da bit 0: first loop waits while set, second while clear; status transition exits each loop.
confirmedStatusPolling.semantics: Read derives blanking state from PIC time and resets attribute-controller/PCjr flip-flops. Not a side-effect-free RAM read.

fixedIoDelays.description: OPL writer loops decrement EBX from 6 and 27; port return values do not control the loop exits.
fixedIoDelays.semantics: OPL port reads consume emulated cycles, update I/O-delay bookkeeping and update OPL timers; cannot be removed as generic idle RAM polling.

inspectedNonPollingExamples.reason: Saturates and writes 16-bit sample values, advances sample pointer, decrements finite sample count.
Reads indexed values, updates arithmetic state, writes packed output, advances destination by 320.
Writes output and advances sample/coordinate state and a finite output counter.
Searches a changing array index; exits on match or exhausted index.
Traverses a linked list, changes node pointer, exits on match or null.

limitations: CPU-time estimates are not guest instruction counts. Isolated repeated blocks omit first iterations included in mixed setup/write blocks.
Snapshot opcode starts and instruction boundaries match all sampled forms; operand-only changes between capture and snapshot are not excluded.
Backward-edge candidate intervals overlap and do not prove all paths inside an interval execute; do not sum their costs.
Screen covers sampled 32-bit backward edges up to 4096 bytes, not unsampled code, all 16-bit code, larger call-spanning waits, or every game.
41.46 sampled CPU seconds lack guest caller attribution, although most have host symbols. The confirmed polling cost is not an exact whole-emulator polling fraction.
Snapshot/disassembly is diagnostic only. No loop skipping, game changes, timing changes or production code changes were made.
decision: No measured dominant RAM polling loop justifies an acceleration implementation. #57 should assess a no-go for generic skipping on this evidence; keep audio/helper costs separate and continue the other measured investigations.
